chapters.summary: Brewer asks what dates the next report will cover and when it will be done. Sidahmed says the FY26 report should be completed by the end of the calendar year and will cover the prior fiscal year.
chapters.title: Brewer asks when FY26 Local Law 83 report will be released

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay, I'd love to work on that with you.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Number two, the report that came out in 2.5 was from July 2.4 to June 2.5.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So what dates do you expect to have your report done for this year?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We're in 2.6, obviously.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Right, so the dates the report will cover?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Yeah, so the fiscal year 26.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay, so it'll be coming out hopefully at the end of this fiscal year.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So yeah, the report itself should be done by the end of this calendar year, but it will cover the previous fiscal year.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: 25 to 26 of the fiscal year.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Council Member Ressler.

chapters.summary: Restler thanks Brewer and the ethnic media representatives in the room. He recalls working on the de Blasio executive order and says implementation under Eric Adams did not work well.
chapters.title: Restler thanks ethnic media and recounts de Blasio-era ad-spending order

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Chair Brewer enjoys giving me a hard time at every opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Every opportunity I can.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I will just take this moment to say something nice.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I think this is the first time I actually have the chance to join a GovOps committee hearing since.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I formally chaired this committee, and I can say I can think of no better colleague to chair this committee in this term than Councilmember Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So thank you for your leadership.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I really appreciate it, and I enjoy working with you, especially when you give me a hard time.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I want to just take a moment to thank all of the...

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Representatives from community and ethnic media outlets that have taken the time to join us today, but much more importantly for the work that you do day in and day out to educate and inform your viewers and readers.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: It makes such a difference.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I know it's hard work.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We all know how the local media landscape has really been decimated in recent years, and it is harder and harder to get by.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: But the work you do is so important, and I really appreciate it, and I know everyone here at the council does.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So thank you for everything you do.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: You know, when I worked in the de Blasio administration, I had the chance to contribute and work on the executive order back in 2019 that.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Dedicate that set the goal of, you know, our significant percentage of our ad spending going to ethnic and community media from city agencies.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And the purpose there was in part to stabilize the struggling industry.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I think that particularly under the leadership of Eric Adams,

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: this didn't work very well.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So, you know, I recognize and appreciate that you're not responsible for the failures of the previous administration.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thankfully, we can say previous.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: But I

chapters.summary: Restler says the FY25 report counted $31 million toward community media but $18 million was out of scope, so actual ethnic media spending was 24%, not 57%. He asks Sidahmed to review out-of-scope spending and accurately count in-scope ads.
chapters.title: Restler says FY25 report overstated ethnic media spending at 24%

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I do want to just call out the FY25 report that noted that a total of $31 million in advertising spending toward community and ethnic media, but $18 million of it was deemed out of scope.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So our actual ethnic and community and media spending was 24%, not 57%, as that report had indicated.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Kind of indicated.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Have you done a review of what spending is being recorded is out of scope?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And are you looking carefully at how to lift up the in scope spending so that we're appropriately and accurately counting the community and ethnic media ad spending that we're doing?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thanks for the question.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I really appreciate your focus on this issue as well.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I really do think that when I get the data and I'm able to really examine what different agencies have been spending, looking at that total amount will be really interesting to understand.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I would love to collaborate with council on how we're defining in scope and out of scope.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: It's something that publishers have mentioned to me as well.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: But yes, that is definitely something that I'll be highlighting in my report.

chapters.summary: Restler says social media, job boards, digital displays, and bus shelter ads are not ethnic media advertising. He asks the office not to confuse or inflate those categories when reporting compliance.
chapters.title: Restler clarifies out-of-scope categories and warns against inflated numbers

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I mean, I just, I want to be clear.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Out of scope, things like that are not print, digital, radio, or TV ads, including but not limited to things like social media, job boards, digital displays, bus shelter ads.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: That's not ethnic community and ethnic media advertising, right?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So we just shouldn't be confusing ourselves or counting it as community and ethnic media advertising when it explicitly isn't.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I just want to make sure that moving forward, we're really clear about what we're doing and what we're not doing so that we're not inflating numbers inaccurately.

chapters.summary: Restler praises Sidahmed's commitment not to politicize ad spending but notes persistent allegations under Adams. He asks whether the office is reviewing outlets that use AI-generated content without real reporters.
chapters.title: Restler raises politicization fears and AI-generated outlets receiving city ads

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I also really appreciated your comments in response to Councilmember Murano's questions that you strongly,

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: you're committed to not allowing for our community and ethnic media advertising to be politicized because it is the role of these reporters to hold the powers that be accountable, whether it be the council or the mayor, and ad spending should not be correlated to that in any way.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I will say that there were persistent and chronic allegations of that happening in the Adams administration.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So I think how you formalize that is really important.

chapters.summary: Sidahmed says determining publication quality could invite accusations of favoritism. He wants a broad public conversation about what fulfills Local Law 83's spirit and sustains civic journalism.
chapters.title: Sidahmed says office must define quality carefully and convene broad conversation

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Relatedly, I'm concerned that ads have been placed in outlets that are heavily dependent on AI, AI-generated content.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I've seen these outlets that claim to be a Bronx outlet, and it's all AI-generated material.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: There's no actual reporters working there.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: There's no actual independent content being created by real journalists, and yet the city is spending ad revenue on it.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Is this something that's on your radar?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Have you conducted an analysis here?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thanks for bringing that up.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And yeah, generally for your focus on this issue, I really appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I think that one of the interesting things with this role and how we're thinking about building this office moving forward is how much does the office

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: really get into determining the quality of the different publications?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Because that could lead to some of the accusations that we heard from the other council members.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So really what I want to do.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: do is, as I mentioned to the chair, convene a group where we can really have a broad conversation about how we're defining what community and ethnic media is,

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: what we want to, what really fulfills the spirit of Local Law 83, and how we're ensuring that

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: We're supporting publications that are giving us that second benefit.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: What is that second benefit?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: It is keeping New Yorkers civically engaged, having reporters show up to hearings like this, having reporters go to community board hearings, go to NYPD hearings.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Really, are they doing that work for their community?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And are New Yorkers better off from this organization being sustained?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And is it helping agencies get the word out there about their publications?

chapters.summary: Restler says real community outlets should be eligible for funding and that hyperlocal reach matters even without huge impressions. He cites Greenpointers as the best way to reach Greenpoint and asks the office to value that in ad selection.
chapters.title: Restler urges valuing hyperlocal reach like Greenpointers

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Yeah, look, I...

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I just, I hope that it's, I think that sounds reasonable.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I hope as you embark on that process that you focus on making sure that real community and ethnic media outlets

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: are the entities that are eligible for receiving this funding, that we're actually using these resources to not just reach New Yorkers and inform New Yorkers about the work of city agencies and opportunities to access services and benefits, but that we're also stabilizing the...

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: The community ethnic media outlets that are actually doing the critical journalism and engaging in their constituencies day in and day out.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: You know, and I just, I imagine that as you, you know, update or consider the firm select, the ad firm selection process and

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: you know, that you're thinking about how many impressions does something get?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: You're thinking,

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: about how effective a given outlet is at reaching specific constituencies.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I just want to say from the vantage point of a parochial council member, I represent Greenpoint.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Greenpointers is like if you want to reach the people in Greenpoint, you go to Greenpointers.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And it's not...

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: That Green Pointers may reach the people in Queens or the Bronx, and they may not have the most impressions in the world, but if you want to reach that neighborhood, there is no better way to do it than going to go and then working with Green Pointers.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And so I just want to make sure that we're valuing that and considering that as you both think through updating the ad selection process and as well thinking about how we define what a community ethnic media outlet is so that we're actually working to stabilize and support this sector.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Last thing for me.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: The chair will shut me up when she needs to, which is often, I promise you.

chapters.summary: Restler asks whether reduced public-notification requirements in ballot questions could hurt local outlet ad revenue. Sidahmed says he is not familiar with the issue and will follow up.
chapters.title: Restler asks about ballot-question public-notice changes and ad revenue

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: The last question for me is that are you concerned that the decrease in public notification requirements proposed in the ballot questions is going to significantly impact

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: ad revenue for local outlets?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Have you looked at this?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'll have to follow up with you on that.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Have you heard from community and ethnic media publications about this and how this is going to impact their revenue?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: As I mentioned, I have to follow up with you about that, and I'm not familiar with it, and publishers haven't reached out to me about it, but it does sound like something I'd be very interested in learning more about.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I am really looking forward to working together.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Appreciate a fresh perspective and some integrity in this office and, you know, excited for the work ahead.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Council Member.

chapters.summary: Brewer says agencies can become lax without leadership and asks how Sidahmed will monitor waivers and claims that agencies spend under $5,000. Sidahmed says he will learn from agencies and reduce friction.
chapters.title: Brewer asks how Sidahmed will push agencies and track waivers

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'm going to call on Council Member Wilson in a minute.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: My other question, though, is just back to these agencies, because I assume that they've been kind of lax where there hasn't been any leadership in your agency.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So at the same time that you are, you know, talking roundtable to the publishers,

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I work in agencies, just as Councilmember Ressler has, and they can get real lazy if nobody is pushing them.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I know exactly how that goes.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So I guess my question is, how are you going to work with these agencies?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I mean, do they qualify for the full mandate waiver?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Are they really under $5,000 for their advertising budget?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: You know, are they, I don't, you know, they could not want to have to have any more mandates.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So they'll tell you it's $5,000.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And even though it's a lot larger, and then the number of agencies which have a full mandate waiver change per year, how do you keep track of them, et cetera.

chapters.summary: Brewer presses on agency follow-through and training. Sidahmed says he has seen excitement from agencies and sees his role as making it easier for them to work with community media.
chapters.title: Sidahmed says agencies are eager to collaborate

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: How are you going to...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Do all that because these agencies can be as challenging as you know people on the outside to be honest with you thank you so much jay i'm new so maybe i have uh um

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: naive optimism but i've i've seen so much excitement about from agencies about collaborating work with me and about getting their messages out to through community and ethnic media that um

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: so many of these agencies are really um excited to collaborate and have been willing to work with me.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I really see my role as making that as frictionless as possible, helping the agencies understand which publications will be great conduits for their messages, depending on the different communities that they want to reach.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: As the council member mentioned, you know, if you're trying to reach people in the Bronx, if you're trying to reach a specific ethnic community, which publications they can look up in the citywide marketing directory to find that can really help them meet their goals.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: That's really my mission.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I've seen a lot of willingness and excitement to do that in my first few weeks on the role.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Councilmember Wilson.

chapters.summary: Wilson asks how the city measures campaign reach and whether ethnic media ads increase awareness or use of city services. Sidahmed says he wants impact stories beyond traditional metrics and that media placement agencies handle campaign-level measurement.
chapters.title: Wilson asks how city measures whether ad campaigns reach intended communities

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And again, echo my colleagues in congratulating you.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Your appointment.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: We're touching on this, but how does the city measure whether its advertising campaigns are actually reaching the communities they're intended to serve?

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And does the mayor's office track whether advertising in ethnic and community media leads to greater awareness of use of city services?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you so much for that question.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I think that's really one of the goals that I would like to lay out in the vision for this office is those stories of impact that you're looking for and that you're mentioning.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I would love to work with publishers to uplift stories of impact where, you know, publishing and advertising campaign around vaccinations with the publisher actually led to more Pakistani New Yorkers getting vaccinated.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: If the publishers can really, we can move beyond the kind of traditional metrics that I think a lot of brands might use for measuring their campaigns.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: But on the individual campaign fronts, I think that the media placement agencies are really responsible for working with the agencies on that.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: But I think my office can play a really great role in making just a broader case for the importance and the value and the impact of community and ethnic media.

chapters.summary: Wilson asks what the office is doing to ensure smaller publications can compete for city advertising. Sidahmed says the office will increase transparency about agency spending and work with placement vendors to include small outlets.
chapters.title: Wilson asks how smaller ethnic publications get fair access to ad funds

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And so many of, as you know, many smaller ethnic and community newspapers serve residents who don't get their news from major outlets.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: What steps is the mayor's office taking to ensure the smaller publications have a fair opportunity to receive city advertising funding?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So really, that's the goal of this office.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: is to ensure that small publications have a clearer understanding of the steps towards getting access to those dollars.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So working with the publishers to just create more transparency about how agencies are spending, where agencies are spending, which media placement vendors are holding which campaigns, really trying to make that process really clear.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And then also working with the placement vendors additionally to help them understand that this is really important and that working with a small publication might be more complicated than a typical big buy,

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: but that they really need to do that and that we as the government see value in that.

chapters.summary: Wilson asks how the city would verify agency attestations under Intro 1129 rather than relying only on self-reporting. Sidahmed says he is not familiar with the proposal and will follow up after reviewing it.
chapters.title: Wilson asks how city would verify agency compliance under Intro 1129

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And then just to one of the bills we're considering today, Intro 1129, the agencies would have to confirm when they've complete certain requirements established by local law.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: So how would the city verify that these requirements have actually been completed rather than relying only on the agency's confirmation?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I'm not familiar with the resolution that you're referring to, so I'd have to follow up with you.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It's proposed.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It hasn't passed yet.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the proposal that you're referring to, but I'm happy to follow up with you once I have a chance to review it.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I'm good, Chair.

chapters.summary: Brewer says agencies may not know what is expected and asks whether Sidahmed will develop training materials and roundtables. Sidahmed says the law mandates annual training and he will build materials after understanding prior agency relationships.
chapters.title: Brewer presses Sidahmed on training materials and urgency for agencies

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I've been joined by Council Members Felice and Council Member Stevens.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'll call on Council Member Stevens in a minute.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'm still focused on these agencies.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I know they have nice, wonderful, sunny ideas, but they still don't always do what you might want them to do.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So are you going to work with training materials?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Don't forget there's a lot of new people, so they may not have the background to know what you are hoping to achieve.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So are you going to do training materials with them?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Are you going to do roundtables?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: How are you going to get them to actually do their job, even though you say they're so excited about this?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you for that question, Cher.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I really want to spend the first few months of my role understanding what their experience has been like with MOECM in the past, especially the agencies that maybe have struggled to meet the 50% or agencies that have large ad budgets.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Really understand what was the friction, what was your experience working at MOECM, how can I reduce that friction?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Once I get an understanding of that, and hopefully we can maybe change some processes and reduce that friction slightly, I'd love my training to be focused on the value and impact that working with these publications provides.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So really getting understanding of what are the communication goals of all the different government agencies and focus the training to be tailored towards that particular agency and help them understand that, okay, you typically work on these five or six campaigns.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Here's how community and ethnic media can.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: really help you achieve those goals.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Let's sit down and work together and think about how you can build a media plan and maybe even bring some publishers in who can help them, help explain to them what their publication does, who it reaches, and how it can be helpful.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So are you going to develop training materials?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Is that also part of your...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Vision or is this something how are you going to actually implement this training that's what i mean yeah so the the law mandates that i have to train every agency um every uh

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: fiscal year i believe and i think the um part of my job in the next few weeks is really going to be

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: building those materials but i do think i don't want to build them without really understanding how things were done previously and what people's relationships i understand that i just i'm concerned because i want to get the money out the door because

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: you and I could be learning and they could be folding because they don't have funding.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So that's why I was asking these agency questions.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Council Member Stevens.

chapters.summary: Brewer says the out-of-scope issue matters because the media world has changed since 2021. She asks why social media advertising is excluded; Sidahmed says he will review how predecessors defined in-scope and out-of-scope spending.
chapters.title: Brewer asks why social media advertising is out of scope under Local Law 83

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay, all right.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: This out-of-scope issue is mostly concerning because it's a different world than when it was when the law was implemented.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So I guess this would come down to what it is that a community and ethnic media outlet is when you have figured out their new or not new definition.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: But social media advertising is considered out of scope.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Is that because of the law or is there some other reason?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I would have to really look back at my predecessors and how they defined the in-scope versus out-of-scope piece.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: But I think that what I really want to do, first of all, is get all of the data for FY26, understand how spending was laid out for the previous fiscal year,

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: and then build a definition around that and understand how agencies are spending.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: But really, ultimately, the goal is to increase the amount of dollars that are going to community and ethnic media.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: That's the ultimate goal for this office and I'd love to collaborate with City Council in finding solutions for that.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Council Member Stevens?

chapters.summary: Stevens says ethnic media groups feel excluded from ad dollars and conversations. She asks how Sidahmed will conduct outreach to print and other traditional outlets as he builds his plan.
chapters.title: Stevens asks how MOECM will reach all outlets and ensure a seat at the table

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I guess some of my questions is I know in conversations with some of the ethnic media groups, they have

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: expressed their concerns about not being able to get access to some of the advertisement dollars or feeling like they're not part of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And maybe you've kind of already addressed some of this.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: What are some of the steps you plan to take to ensure that you're doing outreach to all the different outlets and making sure that they have a seat at the table and also like traditional media print and those things.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: How are you going to make sure that they're engaged in this process as you are building out your plan?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you for the question, Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I've spent the first few weeks of my job sitting down with publishers.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I've met a dozen publishers who represent about 60 news outlets in the city.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I'm looking forward to continuing to do that work, listening to publishers and really making it clear that my office is accessible to them, that they have my phone number, they can call me and we can build a long term relationship.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I think that, you know, as a journalist myself, I feel that people want to be doing the job of journalism.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And a lot of these publications, the journalists are also the publisher who's running, who's trying to get ad dollars.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I want to make that as frictionless as possible and really make myself accessible, make it easy to meet with me, not make it so that everyone has to come to City Hall.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I can go and meet them where they're at and hear from them about their needs.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And as I get a better understanding of everything that's happening internally, really try and create more transparency so people understand how they can get access to these ad dollars.

chapters.summary: Stevens says she represents one of the city's largest and fastest-growing African communities and asks why outlets like Little Africa have received no advertising dollars this year. Sidahmed says he cannot speak to prior media plans.
chapters.title: Stevens asks why Little Africa and African outlets have no ad dollars this year

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So I represent one of the largest African communities in the city, and they're growing fast.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And so one of the questions that I have is also, why is African outlets such as Little Africa and others not received, haven't received any advertising dollars for this year yet?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: If this is something that is a priority.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you for the question.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I can't speak to what was happening before I arrived and the media plans, what was happening before I arrived, but I am really excited to dig into the data for FY26.

chapters.summary: Stevens asks how long it will take to understand ad spending and whether outlets must wait until year-end. Sidahmed says he hopes to finish the report by the end of the year.
chapters.title: Stevens asks how long publishers must wait for FY26 spending data

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: How long is that going to take?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I'm hoping to have the report.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I'm confident I'll have the report done by the end of this year.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So, so.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I just want to make sure I understand.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So because you just started, folks have to wait until the end of the year to figure out how they're supposed to access.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So how do we ensure that these outlets don't collapse in the meantime while you are getting acclimated?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: What was the transition like?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Because that's unfair that because you started that everyone has to wait.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So what is the transition?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: What does that look like?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I'm confused.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Are you the only person there?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Was no one there before?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Like, I'm confused.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I appreciate the question.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So are you asking with the transition into my role?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I do because you just said that it's going to take you about to the end of the year to figure out how these folks are going to get access to the advertising dollars.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And I'm saying that by the end.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: they probably already folded and collapsed.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand what was the transition from you, from the person before you and the staff that's currently there.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Are they not there?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Because I'm not understanding why it's going to take that long because that's not fair to the folks who are waiting for it.

chapters.summary: Stevens presses on the transition and whether outlets will collapse while the office gets acclimated. Sidahmed repeats that he cannot speak to what happened before he arrived.
chapters.title: Sidahmed says he cannot speak to pre-arrival decisions

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I can't speak to what was happening before I arrived.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I really do appreciate the question and your advocacy for community and ethnic media.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I think my first job really is getting an understanding of what happened in the previous three weeks.

chapters.summary: Stevens asks when Sidahmed started and says a year-end timeline is unfair to publishers. Sidahmed says he started three weeks ago and is focused on the report about past spending.
chapters.title: Stevens presses on three-week tenure and outlets waiting for help

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So when did you start?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Three weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: You started three weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I also remember there were eight months, nobody in the office, just so you know.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Eight months.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So because this wasn't a priority for the administration, people now have to suffer.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Because I want to be clear, that's the signal that's being sent out.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Whether you started three weeks ago or not, that doesn't mean that the work does not continue.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And so I'm concerned that now folks are suffering because that's going to be a problem.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So I'm really confused about folks waiting to the next steps.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And so is there any way, is there not staff there that you can work with to figure out how to get these advertisement dollars out faster than by the end of the year?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I really appreciate the question.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I think that what I mentioned previously, my previous comment was about the report.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I think really that's what a lot of folks are trying to understand is where the money went, how the money was spent in the last fiscal year, how different agencies allocated their dollars in the last fiscal year.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So by the end of the year, I'm really working on developing that report.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So getting that data from the different media buyers.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: understanding which agencies they work with and then having the agencies verify that information.

chapters.summary: Stevens says publishers cannot reach Sidahmed if the website has no contact information. Brewer offers to help update the site and says she will call the OTI commissioner to get it fixed.
chapters.title: Stevens and Brewer demand contact information on MOECM website

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I have another question.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: How are folks supposed to contact you if there's no contact information on the website?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Because I'm getting intel right now that they don't even have contact information on the website.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I appreciate that question.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I can follow up with you with more information about that, but I've tried to make myself as accessible as possible.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: How do they find you and how do you be accessible if there's no contact information?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'm going to help you update your website if you want.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It has to be updated.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I know how to update websites.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: You can't say that you want people to reach out to you and you're accessible if they don't have the information.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Please update the website.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'll get the commissioner of OTI to do it for you.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Literally, I'm calling her.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I've noticed since she's born.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I will get that website updated.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair.

chapters.summary: Stevens says the office sat without a leader for eight months and now publishers must wait again. She says the administration moves quickly on its priorities and that this response signals ethnic media is not a priority.
chapters.title: Stevens says office's eight-month vacancy shows lack of urgency

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I mean, I guess I'm done with my time.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I just want to be clear.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Like, I don't think that it's fair that folks have to wait.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Take as long as you want, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Oh, sure.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Don't give me an inch.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I just don't think that it's fair that this office sat without someone to point to for eight months, and now folks still have to wait.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Like, I think the sense of urgency, and this is, it seems like a running theme because I had a hearing yesterday, and a sense of urgency does not seem to be there.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And, you know, I think that when there's issues that the administration deems important, they move mountains to get things done.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And this is a sense of urgency because these.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: These outlets are going to fold, and they depend on this.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: This is their lifeline.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And it's not okay for us to kind of just say that we're going to assess and figure it out.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: That should have been done.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And even if there's not someone at the helm, if we have agencies that if someone leaves, everything stops, that's problem number one.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Things should be in place so that doesn't happen.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So I'm disappointed that that happens, and I'm disappointed that these outlets.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Might fold because we are failing them.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And that is a problem for me because, again, when things are deemed important with this administration, things get done.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And this clearly is something that you guys don't deem important, and that's unacceptable to me.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So thank you, and I appreciate all the things you're saying and understanding that this isn't your fault because you just started three weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: But that is really unfortunate.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I totally agree.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I think that the contact would be half of the equation just in terms of showing good faith.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And then secondly, the issue that I brought up earlier of who is going to be on the list has to move as quickly as possible so that her organizations and others can get funding.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: But I did note that in 25...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Then Comptroller Lander did a report and even had organizations like 1010 Winds and New York One on the community and ethnic media list.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So, I mean, that's, I don't know, to me that would not be community and media list.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: eligible.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: But that's, again, you're going to have to figure that out as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Rather have Councilmember Stevens'smaller community and ethnic list be on the list.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So as quickly as possible, I would suggest that has to be done.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Councilmember Moran.

chapters.summary: Morano asks who determines whether an outlet qualifies for the citywide marketing directory, whether criteria are public, and whether there is an appeals process. Sidahmed reads the current criteria and says he wants a more public process.
chapters.title: Morano asks who decides directory eligibility and whether appeals exist

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And just to pick up on

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: One of the things that both Chair Brewer and Councilmember Stevens were alluding to, I'd like to get a little bit more clarity on how you get on this list, right?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So your office maintains the citywide marketing directory, which agencies use to identify eligible media outlets.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Who determines whether an outlet qualifies for inclusion?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Are the eligibility criteria public?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And is there a formal appeals process if an outlet is rejected?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you for that question, Councilman.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Yeah, that is one of the most important things in this office.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I can read for you the current criteria that's on the website.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: It's in the law.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So it says, serves a particular communities of people based on native language, race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or immigrant status to

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: target a discrete neighborhood, geographic region, or population within a city rather than the city as a whole, or three, falls within a specifically tailored subject matter as determined by the executive director.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I think that as a member of the media previously and in my conversations with publishers, the folks from Nycolum, the New York City

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: local community and ethnic media group are here.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So many publishers have expressed confusion about this list.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And that's why I do think creating a much more public policy and approach to this and having a public conversation so that there isn't confusion about which publications are in and which publications aren't,

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I think is really one of my main goals for this office.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And as I said, I think it can really be a model for the rest of the country as well.

chapters.summary: Morano poses a hypothetical: a 50-year-old paper with original reporting versus a new AI-driven or press-release operation serving the same audience. Sidahmed says he wants a community conversation about those standards.
chapters.title: Morano asks whether legacy and AI/press-release outlets are treated alike

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And we're all rooting for you, I think.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I mean, and we're wishing you the best of luck with that goal.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Let me give you a hypothetical.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Say there are two neighborhood newspapers that serve essentially the same audience, right?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: One's been around.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: That and I, Elaine.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: One's been around for 50 years, has a small staff, and publishes original reporting.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: The other is sort of what Councilmember Ressler was alluding to earlier, a relatively new operation that either uses AI or just mostly republishes press releases.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Are they treated identically for purposes of your directory?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Does original reporting count for anything, or is it strictly a question of reaching a particular audience?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: It's a great, I really just want to say thank you for the question and the level of detail and thought around this issue.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: But I do think this, as I said, is something that I want to be made as a community.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I really do want us to convene a conversation that includes publishers, independent voices, people like yourself who have detailed understanding of this problem.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Because I do think that the question of the agencies being able to reach the most people through these community media outlets and ensuring that we're sustaining that civic function

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: that I mentioned in my testimony are two really important pillars and goals and live up to the spirit of local law 83, which I think is critical.

chapters.summary: Morano asks whether the office would publish how many outlets apply, how many are rejected, and why. Sidahmed commits to follow up after developing a transparent process.
chapters.title: Morano asks for public data on directory applications and rejections

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And would you support, and I'm guessing you would based on everything we've heard today, publishing how many outlets apply to join the directory, how many are rejected, and the reasons for rejection.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I will definitely follow up with you once we have those conversations and, you know, really.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: about what a robust, transparent process looks like for this directory.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I think really, I just generally, I think that one of the goals for me in this role is to increase transparency of this office as a whole.

chapters.summary: Morano asks whether the office tracks ad spending by the communities an outlet serves rather than its headquarters, and how many Staten Island outlets are in the directory. Sidahmed says he will follow up with the data.
chapters.title: Morano asks how Staten Island outlets are tracked and counted

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I have to maintain my reputation with Chair Brewer by asking a Staten Island-focused question.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So you've talked about reaching underserved communities, and I totally agree with that objective.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I represent the South Shore of Staten Island, where a lot of residents rely on neighborhood publications that the larger citywide media rarely pay attention to.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Does your office track advertising expenditures based on the communities an outlet actually serves rather than simply where its headquarters happens to be?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I mean, and further as a kind of a second question there, can you tell me how many Staten Island based or Staten Island focused media outlets are currently in the directory?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you for that question, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I can definitely follow up with you on the second half of the question and get you that information.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And on the first half of the question, I would also need to follow up with you just to really get an understanding of how we would define that.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I think it's really important, though, what you're raising is that who are we reaching with citywide marketing dollars?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: You know, are they I think when this law was created, the majority of the money was not going to community and ethnic media, which is going to really large publications.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So part of the role of this office is really helping city government understand who are we reaching when we spend with community and ethnic media.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So in line with that, I think there is potentially a role for that, and I'd love to follow up with you.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Well, you've got a partner in me.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Brewer asks whether the city has master contracts with ad firms like Greystone or Miller and how Sidahmed will evaluate the six vendors. Sidahmed says he will get contract details from DCAS and partner with the Council on evaluation.
chapters.title: Brewer asks about master contracts and evaluation of six ad firms

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We've been joined by Councilmember Dinowitz.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I have one more question.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We asked earlier about the ones who are the primary advertising firms to help place the ads.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And I know you said that that's still part of your discussions, and there are six of them.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: But does the city have master contracts?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: With Greystone or Miller, and are there master agreements with the other ones?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And I think I said there are six.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So how are you going to make this decision as to who to engage with?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And do you know how long these contracts are for?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I'm happy to follow up with you with that particular information and get you the details of that from DCAS.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: But I do think that the...

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Way in which we're working with the vendors is such a critical part of making sure that local law 83 succeeds.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: They're really a linchpin in ensuring that we work with the community and ethnic media and, you know, from the agency side, creating a more frictionless process and also from the publisher side, feeling like not only are they receiving

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: support, but they're being treated with respect and they're actually getting the things that they, um,

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: that they need and able to do reporting in a way that the agency finds useful.

chapters.summary: Brewer asks how the office will evaluate the six media placement vendors. Sidahmed says the office's role in evaluation still needs discussion and he will follow up once he understands the contracts.
chapters.title: Brewer asks how Sidahmed will judge whether ad vendors do their jobs

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So how are you going to evaluate them?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I assume you haven't had a chance to meet with all six of them yet, but how are you going to evaluate whether or not they're doing their job?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I would love to partner with you on that and what role this office should play in that evaluation.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I think that when we're thinking about the scope of Local Law 83 and what this office is responsible for and what it does, I think that that kind of evaluation is something that we'll need to discuss.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: But I'm happy to follow up with you once I have more information about how the contracts are structured and what we can do moving forward.

chapters.summary: Brewer asks whether Sidahmed hopes to hire additional people beyond one staffer. Sidahmed says the office will evaluate its needs and strategy over the next few months before building a team.
chapters.title: Brewer asks whether MOECM will hire more staff

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I know you mentioned that you're going to hire an additional person.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Are you going to hopefully have others hired, or it's not clear yet?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I believe that what we're hoping to do over the next few months, or sorry, what we are going to do over the next few months is really evaluate the needs for this office, the strategy and how we want to execute on this office, and then build a team that reflects those needs.

chapters.summary: Stevens says the New York Coalition for Ethnic and Community Media feels left out of conversations and sometimes disfavored by the administration. She asks how Sidahmed will engage groups that push the envelope.
chapters.title: Stevens asks about engagement with NY Coalition for Ethnic and Community Media

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Councilmember Stevens.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Sorry, I just had a question.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Specifically, the New York Coalition for Ethnic and Community Media, they're saying that what is the engagement going to look like with them because they feel like they have not been part of a lot of these conversations and specifically

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: because sometimes I guess they're not necessarily seen in good light from the admin.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: What does that look like with, you know, ethnic media groups who might be pushing the envelope, which technically they're supposed to do because that's what media is supposed to do, be the check on government.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And so could you talk about, like, what is your approach is going to be with those outlets?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: My approach with all outlets will be the same.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I'm really excited to meet as many publications as will meet with me from the citywide marketing directory.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I'm having sit-down meetings with a number of publications and publishers.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Publishers are also busy and, you know, scheduling time.

chapters.summary: Stevens asks if Sidahmed has scheduled roundtables or conversations with publishers. Sidahmed says he has spoken to about a dozen publishers and has more meetings scheduled.
chapters.title: Stevens asks whether outreach to publishers has already started

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Have you already started reaching out to them?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Have you scheduled roundtables and conversations with them?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Has that already started?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Yes, I've spoken to about a dozen publishers so far, and I have a number of meetings coming up in the next few weeks with other publishers, and they've been really informative.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So as I said, I'm really excited to have the way that this office functions moving forward, be informed by conversations with publications and really trying to capture the range and diversity of publications that we have.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: in the city, folks who are hyper-local focused on a specific geographic region, or people who focus on a specific language group, or a specific group based on sexual orientation or disability.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And the needs of the different types of publications based on their medium and size really varies, and their relationships with MOECM in the past and what they'd like to see in the future is also quite diverse.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I think that the goal really is to listen to as many publishers as possible and try and understand those through lines and then explain to folks how we want to work moving forward.

chapters.summary: Stevens says media must hold government accountable even when it is adversarial and urges Sidahmed to meet the coalition. Sidahmed says as a former reporter he respects adversarial journalists and will meet them.
chapters.title: Stevens urges outreach to adversarial outlets; Sidahmed pledges access

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Okay, well, I want to just uplift that.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: You should definitely reach out to the New York Coalition of Ethnic Community Media because, you know, they feel like they haven't been a part of these conversations.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And I do think that we want to make sure that we have a diverse group, even if they might seem adversary, because the media's job is to push government and hold us accountable.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And so making sure that we are reaching out to all of those who might not necessarily be as friendly, because that's what the media is supposed to do, hold us accountable.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I really appreciate you raising that, Council Member, and I just want to be super clear.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I was a reporter, so I have a lot of respect for reporters who are adversarial, and I have no issues with meeting with reporters who are adversarial in any way.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I'm more than happy to meet with publishers.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: If I could reach out to your office and be connected to them, I would love to do that.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And to the Council Member's previous questions, I really...

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: do want to make clear that people's coverage of the administration in no way impacts their relationship to this office.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Yeah, I just want to be clear.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Like, I'm an elected official.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I want the people to hold me accountable.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: That's...

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: If everyone is just saying I'm doing a great job,

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I'm scared because you're not pushing my thinking.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And so we need media to make sure that they are actually a check on us and being the voice of the community in the same way I'm the voice of the community.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And so wanting to make sure that everyone has a chance and opportunity, even if they may seem adversarial.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Because, again, like I talk to everyone, even when I don't want to, but we should be talking to everyone.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And that's the media's job.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So I just wanted to make sure that that was taken into consideration.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So thank you.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member.

chapters.summary: Brewer asks how the other 50% of agency ad spending could go to influencers or out-of-scope outlets and whether the definition of community media should change. Sidahmed says his focus is increasing in-scope dollars to directory publications.
chapters.title: Brewer returns to influencer spending and definition of community media

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I have the number.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We'll be glad to share for the coalition.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: They're wonderful.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We're just back to this influencer issue because obviously Department of Sanitation, as an example, they have a budget.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I assume it's more than $5,000.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So they would be one of the agencies that would, in fact, have.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Come under local law 83.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So they will do, I assume, hopefully 50% for the list that you come up with that you will hopefully have done by the end of the year.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Hopefully they've been spending up to now, even though they don't necessarily have a complete list.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: But then the other 50%, would that go if they want to use influencers or other out-of-scope individuals?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: How would you have any sense of that?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Or do we keep that other 50% as their decision?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: But in the world that's different than it was.

chapters.summary: Brewer notes some community media figures may also be influencers and asks how Sidahmed is thinking about the definition. Sidahmed says he wants agencies to understand that community publications serve their communication goals.
chapters.title: Brewer asks whether community media definition should change for influencers

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: was in 2021, is there any change in the definition of what a community and media outlet is?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Or is that something you're going to kind of stick to?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Because some of these media and community folks are probably influencers and a community and media outlet.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Who knows?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So I'm just wondering, again,

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'm coming back to this definition is perhaps different than it was in 2021.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And how will you be looking at that?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Not to say that you're going to make a final decision, but how are you thinking about that?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I appreciate that question, Cher.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I think really, as I've mentioned, my focus is trying to increase the amount that the agencies are spending with the publications in the citywide marketing directory.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So that in-scope number, whatever it might be, however we want to slice it, I really want to ensure that publishers feel like they're getting their fair share and that they're able to continue to

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: grow their publications and do the critical job of journalism that they're doing in the city.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I think that that's really my focus and helping the agencies understand the value of working with these publications, that this isn't something you just have to do because of the local law.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: No, this serves your interests.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: This is critical to you to actually execute on your vision for what you want to accomplish with your agency and your marketing communication goals.

chapters.summary: Brewer raises the possibility of a future health crisis, hurricane, or census and asks whether Sidahmed is planning with emergency agencies. Sidahmed agrees community media are critical conduits and says he will make that case to agencies.
chapters.title: Brewer asks Sidahmed to plan for emergency and census outreach

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: The other question I have is just...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: A little bit hypothetical, but God forbid we have some other crisis.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Office of Emergency Management would obviously...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: kick in, but I'm just wondering if you're, you know, this is not a hopeful thing, but there's always something that comes up in our city.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And I'm just wondering if you're meeting with them just to say that if in fact there is some crisis, it could be a health crisis, it could be a hurricane, it could be, you know, something beyond imaginable.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Meeting with them to say if such a thing happens, how could we work together to get the word out?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: In other words, obviously there would have to be increased advertising budget in certain communities.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So are you thinking along those lines also?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I think that there are, you know, in a lot of the communities that the publication serves, we're already in a state of emergency and crisis for a lot of communities in New York City right now.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I think that ensuring that they're getting critical information out to the communities that these publications serve is critical.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And really trying to ensure that marketing directors at all the agencies understand the importance and that these are your best conduits for trying to get information out to all New Yorkers is something that is incredibly important.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I will be making that case.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And the example of the pandemic is really important.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I think there's a turning point for many folks around, you know, how Executive Order 47 kind of coming into and being written right before the pandemic.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I think really was what set the stage for local law 83.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I wasn't in government.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I would love to partner with you and understand how that works and how if something like that was to happen again, we can learn from that experience and try to...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Not a panic, but the census could be a panic if this president decides how he's going to handle it and we don't.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So that's an example.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It's a situation where we absolutely need every single outlet to be available and clear.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And so that's an example.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And 2030 is not so far away.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I couldn't agree more.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz says his district lost the Norwood News and asks what the office does or can do to support local media. Sidahmed calls the closure devastating and says the office works on the sector as a whole.
chapters.title: Dinowitz asks how MOECM can help after Norwood News closure

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Councilmember Denowitz.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I think you had just made reference to some of the local newspapers.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And in my district, we actually lost a local newspaper, the Norwood News.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Have you heard of this?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: If you could just share some of the work that your office does or can do, because as we're losing papers, we're also losing a critical part of our civic structure.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: What work your office does to support our local media and what further work you can do and investments you can make to bring back the Norwood News?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I appreciate that question.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I think everyone in local media was devastated to hear about the loss of Norwood News.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: It was the breeding ground for a lot of great Bronx journalists and is a publication that I think was near and dear to many people's hearts.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So we were all devastated to hear about that.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And it speaks to the broader trend that I've spoken about in my testimony of the different.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: conditions that we're currently under to keep local news alive.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So that is really the whole entire purpose that this office was created for and why Local Law 83 was put into place was to help preserve these community institutions like the Norwood News.
