chapters.summary: Dinowitz says the Norwood News has not been preserved and asks what work the office has done to bring it back. Sidahmed says the office helps agencies understand where to spend more with local publications.
chapters.title: Dinowitz presses how to bring back Norwood News

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Well, I know I understand that, but it has not been preserved.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So I'm wondering how we can work together to preserve it.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Or what work, if any, the office has done to bring back the Norwood News.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So specifically on specific publications, I think the goal of the office is really to work on the sector as a whole

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: and try and help agencies understand that they should be working with the publications in this sector in order to achieve their goals.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So really what I'm trying to do as we start in this role and build out this office is work with the different agencies to help them understand where they're spending and how they can be spending more with publications.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: They can both meet their goals of getting the word out to the communities that really need this information and also help sustain publications in the city that are critical for our

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: civic infrastructure.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz asks whether agency marketing directors know the Norwood News is gone and only the Riverdale Press remains. Sidahmed says he cannot speak for every director but sees educating agencies as part of his role.
chapters.title: Dinowitz asks whether agencies know only Riverdale Press covers Northwest Bronx

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So in your assessment, do you think the agencies are aware that there's only one local newspaper that covers the Northwest Bronx?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: That's the Riverdale Press.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Because the Norwood News is no longer there?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: So I couldn't speak to their kind of understanding of all the different

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: marketing directors in all of the different agencies and some of them are former journalists themselves and I'm sure you know maybe worked in the Bronx themselves I wouldn't want to completely say that no marketing director in New York City government is aware of that but I do see it as my role

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: to help people understand the urgency of this moment and I guess I'm asking

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: If you're identifying your job as to work with these marketing directors in the different agencies, wouldn't it then also be part of your job to make sure they know about the closure of local media outlets?

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I appreciate the question.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I appreciate the question.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that...

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I do agree that there is a role to be played for helping them understand the Norwood News is a critical source of information for people in the Northwest Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And if you're trying to reach people in the Northwest Bronx, it's critical to work with publications like that.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I hope that all the different agencies.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: In my time in working in this office, will have a deep fluency of all the different publications in New York and will know which publications to work with if they're trying to reach different people in different places.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: And I see my role as trying to educate them and help them understand that.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz says the office should not merely hope agencies understand local media gaps but should treat it as an obligation. Sidahmed thanks him and agrees there is a role for educating agencies about outlets like the Norwood News.
chapters.title: Dinowitz says local news support is an obligation, not hope

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Yeah, I would think you don't just have to hope.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: That they have an understanding.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I mean, I would think that would be part of your job, right?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And so I'm ready to work with you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: To make sure our agencies understand this.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: The Norwood News isn't just critical, a critical publication in Norwood, Bedford Park.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It's the only one.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: That was the only place my neighbors were getting their information.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And now they have nothing.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: There's no other print publication that's delivering to the different buildings, that's in all the centers where people need to get information.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I stand ready to work with you, but I think the perspective should be less about hope and more about obligation.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I think we as a city have an obligation, and in your office have an obligation, to work with these marketing directors as you've identified.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: To support local journalism, particularly those who have or are on the cusp of closing.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

chapters.summary: Brewer thanks Sidahmed and says the committee looks forward to working with him. She announces the hearing will move to the next panel and then public testimony.
chapters.title: Brewer thanks Sidahmed and closes administration testimony

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We look forward to working with you.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We're going to go to the next panel.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Mazen Sidahmed
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Brewer opens public testimony, reminds attendees that decorum must be observed, and bans video or photography from the witness table. She explains that speakers get three minutes and written testimony can be submitted by email within 72 hours.
chapters.title: Brewer opens public testimony and sets three-minute rule

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So I now open the hearing for public testimony.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I remind members of the public that this is a government proceeding and that decorum shall be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Members of the public shall remain silent at all times.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who wish to testify.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: No video recording or photography is allowed from the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Members of the public may...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: may not present audio or video recordings as testimony, but may submit transcripts of such recordings to the sergeant at arms for inclusion in the hearing record.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I just want to say I'll continue, but we're going to call Rachel Faust from Re-Invent Albany and Ben Weinberg for Citizens Union.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Please come to the table.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: If you wish to speak at the hearing, please fill out an appearance card with the sergeant at arms and be recognized.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: When recognized, you will have three minutes to speak at today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Mayor's Office of Ethnic and Community Media and Government Spending on Advertisements.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: That's the title of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: If you have a written statement or additional written testimony you want to submit for the record, please provide a copy of that to the Sergeant at Arms.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: You can also email written testimony to testimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Within 72 hours of the close of the hearing, audio and video recordings will not be accepted.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: If you're here as a panelist in person, please come up to the table once your name has been called.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And we will start with either Rachel or Ben, whoever wants to begin.

chapters.summary: Fauss asks the Council to pass legislation clarifying that electronic communications creating public records must be archived and retrievable. She also asks for a separate FOIL compliance hearing and supports Intros 1127, 1128, and 1129.
chapters.title: Reinvent Albany's Rachel Fauss urges records-retention law and FOIL hearing

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: Ben and I were talking about who should go first, and we were both being too polite, but I'll start.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: My name is Rachel Foss.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: I'm the Senior Policy Advisor for Reinvent Albany.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: Reinvent Albany advocates for transparent and accountable government in New York.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: We're here today to ask...

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: the council to do five things.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: First, pass legislation clarifying that electronic communications that create a public record must be archived and thus easily retrievable by agency FOIL officers.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: And we presented a draft bill in conjunction with Citizens Union at last month's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: While we appreciate that this hearing provides another opportunity to discuss instant messaging retention policies, we do not think creation of a working group in your pre-considered bill is necessary.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: We know that the working group would dissolve after issuing a report.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: It's in line with the council's goals of limiting reporting requirements like the other bills on today's agenda.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: But we do believe our bill to clearly define substantive instant messages and retention rules in the city charter is the best path forward.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: We are concerned that further delay in clarifying these requirements risks losing additional important government communications that should be preserved.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: Second, we asked the council to hold a separate hearing on the Freedom of Information Law compliance and our proposed records retention bill.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: The Department of Records and Information Services told the city reporter this week that their implementation report for Local Law 199, your bill, Chair Brewer, that codifies and expands the open records portal will be released in mid-November.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: Topics are synergistic given that one important goal of records retention is ensuring the public can access records about government decision-making through FOIL.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: We also support and

chapters.summary: Fauss supports consolidating unnecessary agency reports and says Intro 1076's influencer disclosures could fit into the annual advertising report. She also asks the Council to clarify enforcement of the charter ban on electioneering communications.
chapters.title: Fauss suggests folding influencer disclosures into annual ad report

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: the council's initiative to consolidate or eliminate agency reports that are no longer necessary, and we support intros 1127, 1128, and 1129.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: Considering the topic around ethnic and community media today, we continue our ask that intro 1076, which has

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: influencer disclosures could be folded into the annual advertising spending report rather than reside with Doris.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: I think given the conversation today about influencers and ethnic media, there's a lot of overlap and being in the comms office actually makes it might make sense to broaden that report.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: And then lastly, on the topic of paid advertising, we asked the council to look at clarifying enforcement authority for the council, the city charter's ban on electioneering communications paid for with city resources.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: And there's more in my testimony, but my time's up.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Rachel Fauss
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Weinberg says government-paid influencer posts should be clearly disclosed as paid for by the government. He recommends mirroring federal disclosure guidelines and writing the requirement into city advertising contracts.
chapters.title: Citizens Union's Ben Weinberg seeks paid-for influencer disclosure

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Brewer and Council Member Dina Waits.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: My name is Ben Weinberg.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: I'm the Director of Public Policy at Citizens Union.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: I'll make three comments today, two on the topic of the hearing and one on Chair Brewer's bill.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: So first, government spending on advertisements using social media influencer.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: This came up here and at the September hearing.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: We strongly encourage this advertisement to be clearly disclosed.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: When people see an influencer post, they may not realize it's paid for by the government.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: So the council should establish clear paid for by disclosure requirements that mirror federal guidelines, incorporate them into the city's advertising contracts, as the council often does,

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: establishing conditions on city contracts in Title VI, Chapter 1 of the Admin Code.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: So this would be a simple fix.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: We don't recommend addressing this issue by placing restrictions on individual public servants, as was discussed in the last hearing.

chapters.summary: Weinberg says the charter has banned using public resources to influence elections since 1998, but enforcement has eroded. He asks the Council to give COIB explicit authority to issue rules and guidance on the ban.
chapters.title: Weinberg urges limits on electioneering ads and COIB enforcement authority

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: Second, we think the council should limit government spending on advertisement for political and electioneering purposes.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: This also came up in some of the questions by council members.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: So the charter has prohibited using public resources to influence elections and referendum questions since 1998.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: But we've seen in recent years that that prohibition has eroded, especially when we have the legislative branch and the executive branch on on.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: opposite sides of a ballot referendum.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: There are basically no clear guidelines on this issue.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: There's no regulator who decides or guides on who crosses the line and when, and no one who enforces the ban on referendum electioneering.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: Even in recent weeks, we've seen questions and concerns about the ad campaign by City Hall around the ballot questions.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: The truth is we don't really know if those violated the law or not because there's no regulator or watchdog that would tell us whether this does in fact constitute illegal electioneering.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: The conflict of interest toward COIB is best positioned to address this gap, and the council should give the COIB explicit authority to issue rules and provide guidance on the existing prohibition.

chapters.summary: Weinberg cites a DCAS whistleblower lawsuit involving personal phones and private emails used to avoid public records. He says the Council should ban auto-delete functions and codify instant-messaging retention in the charter, calling Brewer's working-group bill a useful first step.
chapters.title: Weinberg urges ban on auto-delete and codified messaging retention

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: Third, on record retention related to the pre-considered by Chair Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: The council needs to ban the use of auto-delete functions from government communications and codify instant messaging record retention policy in the charter.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: This was discussed in September as well, a bit in this hearing as well, but a recent reporting that you all might have seen of a whistleblower lawsuit involving DCAS, where senior

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: managers allegedly used personal phones, private emails, memos to keep sensitive talk out of public record, in one case explicitly opening their text messages by saying, hey, I didn't want this on Teams.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: That further highlights

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: It's why we need to keep this issue, keep clear rules on this issue.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: So, and I'll just mention, I know a lot of time, just mention quickly, at the last hearing, we heard the administration imply that public servants are basically free to choose for themselves

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: whether messages on third-party apps should be retained.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: What messages constitute as substantive communication, what apps they should use for communication.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: So there's obviously a lot of confusion there, to say the least.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: Councilmember Brewer's bill to have a working group led by Doris to study and recommend improvements is a useful first step.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: We appreciate the effort to align the modern use of instant messaging with the city's needs for record retention.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: And public accountability, and to encourage the administration to rethink its position on enforcement in this issue.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: But we also believe the council should go further and prioritize directly amending the charter to address these challenges, establish binding record retention requirements, codify instant messaging message policies, and explicitly prohibit the use of these auto-delete functions.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Brewer thanks Fauss and Weinberg and says the bills they discussed are being drafted but were not ready for this hearing. She says the committee remains focused on them.
chapters.title: Brewer says records and disclosure bills are being drafted

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you both for many years of excellent testimony and support.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I will say that just so you know, all of the bills that you talked about previously in your testimony are being drafted.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It's just a little slower and couldn't get them ready for this hearing, but we're certainly focused on them.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So thank you both very, very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Ben Weinberg
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Davids testifies for the New York Coalition of Ethnic and Community Media and says the office had no leadership, staff, or recourse for nine months. She says publishers could not get answers about disappearing city advertising or Local Law 83 compliance.
chapters.title: NY Coalition's Mona Davids details nine months without MOECM leadership

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Next panel.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: is Mona Davids.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: That's from the group that we loved and was mentioned earlier by Council Member Stevens.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Ms.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: C.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Fawadi Morris, Bob Henley, and Walter Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Go ahead, whoever would like to start.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I don't know where everybody else is, but go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Good morning, Chair Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today on behalf of the New York Coalition of Ethnic and Community Media.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: We want to thank you for having this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: We want to thank you, the Speaker's Office, her team, as well as Simone Jones, the Chief Equity Officer for the City Council, for meeting with us and hearing our cries.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Although the council has touched on, this hearing has touched on the challenges that ethnic and community publishers have faced

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: this year under the Mamdani administration, I think it's really important just to quickly, before I go into our proposed amendments and recommendations for Local Law 83, but just to have it on the record

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: how we have suffered.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: For the general public to understand what's been happening.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: It has not been eight months of no leadership.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: It's been nine months without leadership, staff, or recourse.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: For the first nine months of the Mamdani administration,

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: No one was leading the office of ethnic and community media.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Publishers were left without a fund.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: functioning office, a designated contact, or anyone to answer fundamental questions about the disappearance of city advertising and the city's compliance with Local Law 83.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: During this period, publishers repeatedly sought answers about why advertising that had supported their businesses and helped them serve New York's diverse communities had disappeared.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Their inquiries went unanswered.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: There was no meaningful point of contact, no clear explanation, and no avenue for resource.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: The impact on ethnic and community media publishers has been devastating.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: These are often small independent businesses, including immigrant-owned publications that have spent years building trusted relationships with their communities and sharing information about public services and city programs.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: They provide news and public information in languages and neighborhoods that mainstream media frequently do not reach.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Yet for nine months, publishers were left to confront the loss of advertising without effective leadership or support from the very office established to serve the sector.

chapters.summary: Davids asks the Council to amend Local Law 83 to create an independent office outside the mayor's direct authority. She proposes quarterly public reporting, recipient disclosure, influencer accountability, anti-retaliation protections, stronger 50% enforcement, appeals, audits, and an independent review of 2026 ad allocations.
chapters.title: Davids proposes independent office, quarterly reporting, and anti-retaliation rules

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: I'm just going to briefly outline our proposed recommendations for the office and for amendments to

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Over time, because you have a lot to say.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: The New York Coalition for Ethnic and Community Media calls on the New York City Council to amend Local Law 83

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: of 2021 to establish a transparent, independent, and enforceable system

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: governing city advertising expenditures, the selection of media recipients, and the oversight of advertising agencies and other contractors spending taxpayer funds.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: The proposed amendments should, one, establish an independent office of ethnic and community media outside of the mayor's direct authority.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Require quarterly public reporting by the independent office for every city agency and every contracted advertising agency.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Require disclosure of every recipients of city-funded advertising, including ethnic and community media outlets, influencers, and other digital recipients.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Establish uniform verification, reporting, and accountability requirements for influencers receiving taxpayer-funded campaigns.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Prohibit political favoritism, editorial coercion, and retaliation in advertising allocation and press access.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Strengthen enforcement of the minimum 50% mandate for ethnic and community media advertising and improve waiver oversight.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Establish an independent complaint, appeal, and audit and investigation procedures.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: Require transparent advertising placement criteria and written explanations for exclusions,

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: protect public records and require the preservation of advertising-related communications,

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: and lastly, commission an independent review of advertising allocations since January 1, 2026, including the reported decline by publishers.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: The coalition's position is that the city cannot claim to support ethnic and community media

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: while leaving publishers without an office to contact, an explanation for disappearing advertising, or a process to challenge decisions affecting their livelihoods.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: The law must provide enforceable protections regardless of which administration controls City Hall.

utterances.speaker: Mona Davids
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So thank you so much.

utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.title: URL Media's S. Mitra Kalita says some network publishers got zero city ad dollars in 2026

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We have a saying in Queens that Queen gets the money, so here Walter Sanchez and I am.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: But I would like to introduce myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: My name is Esmitra Kalita.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I live in Jackson Heights, Queens, and I have been a journalist for 30 years covering and leading news teams nationally and locally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I was a senior vice president at CNN, managing editor of the LA Times, executive editor of Quartz, a page one writer for the Wall Street Journal, a reporter for Newsday, the Associated Press, and the Washington Post.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I've also written two books and been honored for my work in newsrooms, including the Pulitzer Prize and the Edward R.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Murrow Award.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: In 2020, I left corporate mainstream media as the pandemic, racial justice protests, and presidential election collided.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: With our democracy in crisis, I decided my efforts might be best applied to local news.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Today, I am the CEO of URL Media, which stands for Uplift, Respect, and Love.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: love, which is a revolutionary idea in media, and the publisher of Epicenter NYC, a community-centered news organization rooted in Queens covering issues citywide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: As CEO of URL Media, I am here on behalf of the New York City publishers in our network, numbering more than a dozen, whose experiences with city advertising admittedly vary widely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Some tell us they have received zero advertising dollars in calendar year 2026.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: That has not been the case for Epicenter NYC, which I also run, but I stand in solidarity with New York City publishers, nonprofit and for-profit, large and small,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: ethnic and mainstream, and veterans of print, broadcast, and digital, just like myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We are stronger together.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: New York needs an ecosystem, not a handful of survivors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Local Law 83 was a pioneering policy, and we've talked about much of the decimation of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: In the interest of time, I'll speed this up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: The implementation has not lived up to the promise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: You have cited the reports showing that spending has fallen 84% since the law took effect, and we've raised concerns about late reporting and the addition of major mainstream outlets to the ethnic and community media directory.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: This distinction matters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: A growing percentage of a shrinking or narrowly defined advertising budget is not a growing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: investment in our communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Translation, you cannot shrink the denominator and call it a success.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I have been sounding this alarm for more than a year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I have raised these concerns with council members, mayoral transition committee members, Governor Hochul's policy advisors, and members of the state senate and assembly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Last December, URL Media and the Center for Community Media tried to get in front of the issue, and we signed an open letter

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: signed by 51 outlets publishing in 14 languages asking the incoming administration to restore spending and transparency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We also made a number of recommendations around some of the issues that have been raised around press passes, access, spend by city-supported institutions on local and ethnic media.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: They're in the appendix.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I don't want to take more time, but I do want to mention that we laid out quite a number of issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We are still today asking for a functioning, predictable, and transparent system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We are thrilled, and I want to be clear about this, by Mazen Sidhamed's appointment to lead the Mayor's Office of Ethnic and Community Media, and we look forward to working with him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: He understands the work, the communities, and the stakes, and the urgency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: His appointment is an opportunity for a reset, but it must also come with the staffing, authority, resources, and accountability necessary to make that reset real.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We are asking this in the middle of a media landscape

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: that has changed dramatically since this law passed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: For example, our audiences are consuming more video now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: AI-generated summaries can draw on our reporting without sending readers back to us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Publishers in our network describe steep web traffic losses, in some cases approaching 40%, and in other cases unknown because of the prevalence of bots and unknown visitors to our websites.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: At the same time, government funding cuts have left community outlets without the money to deliver information and resources to New Yorkers, while the retreat from DEI commitments and pressure on subscriptions and audience reach are hitting multiple parts of our business.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Even those who have diversified our revenue feel under assault.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Creators and influencers are also a part of this changing landscape.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I do not believe we should pit them against established publishers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I do believe we need transparent standards for everyone receiving public advertising dollars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Who was selected?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: What were they paid to deliver?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: And which communities were reached?

chapters.summary: Kalita asks for a clear Local Law 83 recovery plan, quarterly outlet-level reporting, open decision-making, modern measures beyond impressions, and regular engagement with publishers. She says advertising must never reward favorable coverage or punish scrutiny.
chapters.title: Kalita proposes implementation plan, quarterly outlet reporting, and modern metrics

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Today, I am asking for your partnership to modernize the system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Do not make it more opaque.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We also need to reconsider how we talk about ethnic media.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: The term can make us sound peripheral.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: In a city as diverse as New York, where two-thirds of the city is non-white, we are not peripheral to the people we serve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We are New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: At Epicenter, we helped more than 20.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: 20,000 New Yorkers connect to COVID vaccines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: And I just want to take a moment to thank you, Councilwoman, for including links to how to get vaccinated to Epicenter in your weekly communication with your constituents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Our work did not stop at publishing information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Today, we are helping communities understand their rights amid immigration enforcement like we have never seen before in English, Spanish, Bangla, Chinese, and other languages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We do not just tell people a service exists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Community media close the distance between a public promise and a person's ability to use it to gain access.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: That trust is valuable, but it is also labor intensive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Translation, cultural adaptation, answering questions, and community distribution should not be treated as free extras attached to an advertising buy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I'm going to speed this up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I asked the council administration to take five concrete steps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: First, publish a clear implementation and recovery plan for Local Law 83.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Explain how every agency will meet its responsibilities, identify gaps in current outreach, and restore meaningful investment, not simply report a percentage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Second, require quarterly outlet-level reporting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Show the agency's campaign outlets, language, boroughs, or audiences served, the amount allocated, and the amount actually paid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We must report agency and intermediary fees separately from the dollars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Piggybacks on Eleanor Tatum's excellent point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We should include a creator in influencer spending.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: I do want to also mention that the delays in payment from the city results in delays in payment to the agencies, which results in delays or non-existent payroll that our publishers have to meet.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It's a citywide problem.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We're aware of it.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Keep going.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Third, open the decision-making process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Publishers should know who selects outlets, what criteria are used, and whom to contact when an entire language, community, or neighborhood is being missed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Eligibility and placement decisions must be protected from political favoritism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Advertising, as we've discussed, must never be a reward for favorable coverage or withheld as punishment for scrutiny.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Fourth, modernize what the city buys and how it measures value.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We must, as we've discussed today, go beyond the web impression and recognize how publishers deliver on engagement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: For example, through community partnerships and cultural competent outreach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Evaluate whether a campaign reaches the intended residents, not simply whether it generates inexpensive ad impressions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Fifth and finally, establish regular engagement and a broader plan for media resilience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Give this office a dependable mechanism for hearing from publishers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: And yes, the website as they start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Work across city agencies and with state government on complementary policies that support journalism, workforce development, shared...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: production resources, and the transition underway in our industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: New York is held up as a model for community advertising policy, community media advertising policy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: At conferences across the world, I hear praise for our law while knowing how uncertain and interrupted the experience has been for publishers at home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We should be able to stand behind that model, not bite our tongues when it is celebrated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: New York, too, is the media capital of the world.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Remaining so requires more than preserving famous brands.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: It requires sustaining the newsrooms, broadcasters, creators, and community relationships that make this city legible to the people who live here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: This is not a request that government replace our business models or purchase our loyalty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: It is a request that government communicate effectively, spend transparently, pay us fairly for our work, and honor the responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: We need both an ecosystem that sustains this work and an infrastructure that values it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - S. Mitra Kalita
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Wisdom says she founded Harlem Network News during COVID because Black residents were not seeing themselves in media or trusting health information. She asks for immediate investment, inclusion in planning, and contacts for the new MOECM leadership.
chapters.title: Harlem Network News founder Terry Wisdom calls for immediate ethnic media investment

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And the first person is Terry Wisdom.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you, Terry Wisdom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I'm Terry Wisdom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I am the CEO and founder of Harlem Network News.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: And I just want to really show my gratitude to Gail Brewer, our councilwoman, Gail Brewer,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: former Manhattan borough president, and also to our speaker, Julie Minin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: Column Network News started at the onset of COVID.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I have a background in media, 30 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I am in several unions, a video editor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I've worked at every network that you can think of from ABC to NBC to CBS, local news, network news.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: Worked at CNN when they first started.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I was up in Connecticut.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I have worked in feature films.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I am trained.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I have a degree in media from Fordham.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: University, went to Lincoln University, and was part of PBS program that they had for media.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: And I started my career at Sesame Street and Electric Company.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: So I am a media person.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I live, sleep, and breathe it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I'm also a Harlem entrepreneur.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: At the onset of COVID, my partner had been encouraging me to start a network.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: But at the onset of COVID, when I saw Black people walking around Harlem thinking,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: that they could not get COVID because they did not see their images.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: And we know that there are certain diseases that, you know, affect other and certain communities, like a sickle cell mainly impacts people of color.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: But part of it was they were not part of the media conversation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: And because of things like the Tuskegee experiments, they really didn't trust the medical community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: I am proud to say that then our president, Gail Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: Okay, so what I want to say is it's critical with this ethnic media that money be infused.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: It's a to be who is owned by Fox News and they're getting our advertising dollars for our.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: And they will tell you, oh, you know, send us some B-roll and we'll put it on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: They never do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: So I'm ready to stand up and fight back for this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: And it's unacceptable from this administration that has taken this long.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: For us to get ahead of ethnic media.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: Thank you, and I do need to get contacts for the head of the ethnic media so that we can connect, and I appreciate greatly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: This is a breakthrough thing that's happening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: So I love it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Terry Wisdom
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: The Committee on Governmental Operations, State & Federal Legislation held an oversight hearing on the Mayor's Office of Ethnic and Community Media and city advertising spending, along with four good-government reporting bills.

Newly appointed MOECM Executive Director Mazen Sidahmed testified that he is the office's only staff member and is still compiling FY26 ad-spending data, drawing sharp questions from Speaker Menin, Chair Brewer, and committee members.

Ethnic and community media publishers described steep drops in city advertising, months without office leadership or contacts, payment delays, and demanded stronger transparency, enforcement, and independent oversight under Local Law 83.
title: Committee on Governmental Operations, State & Federal Legislation
topic: Oversight - Mayor's Office of Ethnic & Community Media and Government Spending on Advertisements
